newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Kiev invites investors for smaller oil/gas fields.
newsitem.headline: Kiev invites investors for smaller oil/gas fields.

text.p: Ukraine will seek to attract foreign investors to develop a group of smaller oil and gas deposits by holding tenders for the fields in coming months, a government spokesman said on Tuesday.
The spokesman told Reuters that Kiev would award licences and tax and other incentives to investors wishing to drill for oil and gas at hard-to-recover or idled deposits.
The two leading reserves were Bitkiv-Babchynske in western Ukraine and Lelyakivske in the Chernihiv region, some 200 km (110 miles) east of Kiev.
Bitkiv-Babchynske will produce only 46,300 tonnes of oil this year. Some 21,500 tonnes will be pumped at the Lelyakivske deposit, while gas output there is forecast at 3.9 million cubic metres.

"Foreign investors will not lose there -- they would get many privileges," said Stepan Yaloveha, a spokesman for State Oil and Gas Committee, adding that the body would conduct tenders for the deposits in coming months.

Ukraine plans to increase annual national oil output from 4.2 million tonnes (84,000 barrels per day) in 1997 to seven million tonnes (140,000 bpd) by 2010. It consumes about 35 million tonnes (700,000 bpd) of oil annually and imports most of the balance from Russia.
Domestic gas output, forecast at 18 billion cubic metres this year, is due to increase to 35 billion by 2010.
Ukraine consumes 86 bcm each year, including 53 bcm from Russia and up to 15 bcm imported from the Central Asian states of Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.
